thread:
maya: FYI escalation from AcmeCorp — tool/function calling is failing for them after yesterday's model/runtime rollout. They see schema validation errors and some malformed-args failures. They say it started ~09:20 UTC and it's blocking order-processing jobs.

maya: I'm pasting the minimal repro payload they sent and the error. Can someone triage? cc @derek @elena @sam

acme-support: repro payload (redacted):
```json
{
  \"user_id\": 98234,
  \"action\": \"create_order\",
  \"items\": [{\"sku\": \"ABC123\", \"qty\": 2}],
  \"metadata\": {\"promo\": \"SPRING\"}
}
```

acme-support: response we get back from API (400):
```json
{
  \"error\": \"invalid_args\",
  \"details\": \"schema mismatch: field items[0].qty expected integer, got string\"
}
```

maya: but the payload we got above has qty as int. Their code path previously worked. They also reported intermittent extra latency (p99 jumped ~200ms) and one billing anomaly — a sudden jump in token consumption for tool-calls.

derek: looking. two quick q's: which model (catalog id) and runtime version? any recent config changes on their Dedicated pool?

maya: model: open-compat-v2.1, runtime: rtf-1.14.1 (deployed yesterday 03:00 UTC). No customer-side config changes.

derek: thanks. early guess: stricter JSON schema enforcement introduced in rtf-1.14.1 plus a change in tool selection logic that sometimes picks a different tool with a different schema. That could cause the mismatch + token blowup if we add extra system prompts for tool disambiguation.

elena: I see matching exceptions in the runtime logs for their region. Sample log: `ToolCallValidationError: schema mismatch for tool create_order_v2: items[0].qty expected int, received \"2\"` — interesting, that indicates we received a string. Need to capture the exact inbound request bytes.

sam: Acme provided a curl they used to call our API. Asked them to run this and paste output: 
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/responses \
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN\" \
  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \
  -d '{"model":"open-compat-v2.1","input":"<their prompt>","tools":[{"name":"create_order_v2","schema":{"type":"object","properties":{"items":{"type":"array"}}}}],"user":{"id":98234}}'
```

sam: Acme ran it and attached full request/response headers. There are no proxies rewriting body on their side.

derek: can you attach the exact inbound HTTP body (raw) from the runtime? If it's a stringy number we need to find where casting happens. Also I'll run our local repro with their payload.

qa-bot: CI alert: `toolcall-schema-suite` failed on main at 1765001200. First failing test: `order_create_qty_type` — see CI: https://ci.redwood.ai/1765001200/toolcall-schema-suite/results

eval-bot: eval run (golden prompts) shows regression starting at commit b3f9ea7 -> rtf-1.14.1. Failing cases: 14/120 (11.6%). Top failure mode: schema mismatch where numeric fields come through as strings when prompts include templated JSON insertion. Details: https://evals.redwood.ai/runs/2025-06-10/5623

derek: ok reproducer locally: when we build the prompt with templated JSON using our helper `safe_json_insert`, it coerces numbers to strings if the template is passed through the chat formatting helpers. Quick repro script: 
```python
payload = {"items": [{"sku":"ABC123","qty": 2}]}
prompt = f"Process order: {json.dumps(payload)}"
# older helper used raw json.dumps, new formatting pipeline escapes differently -> numbers become strings in the final parsed content
```

elena: that matches. The new tokenizer/escape path introduced a step that serializes dict -> string and then we wrap inside an extra quoted text node. The function-calling parser then parses JSON from the message text and numeric tokens are read as strings because quotes are inserted.

derek: mitigation options: 1) quick runtime rollback to rtf-1.13.x (revert enforcement) 2) hotfix in runtime to canonicalize numeric types when parsing tool args OR 3) add a permissive parse flag `function_calling.permissive_parse=true` that will attempt to coerce numeric strings to numbers for known tool schemas.

elena: we can ship (3) as a config toggle within hours and flip it for Acme's tenant only. We'll also add a logging hook to capture incoming raw message for deeper postmortem. I can prepare a patch: `rtf-hotfix/perm_coerce_nums` and push a canary.

maya: Acme is asking for timeline; they need a temporary workaround. Can we enable flag on their Dedicated pool ASAP?

elena: yes, if they are on Dedicated we can flip per-tenant config. @derek can you review the patch? I'll stage a canary in us-west-2 for 30 minutes and verify with Acme's repro.

derek: will review in 20. Also adding unit tests to cover the templated JSON case — updating `tests/toolcall_schema_suite.yaml` with a golden prompt (from Acme) and expected parsed args. Will push to PR and add to CI.

sam: telling Acme: temporary workaround will be a per-tenant toggle, patching now. Also asked them to run the curl with a slightly different header we requested to capture raw body: `X-Debug-Orig: 1`.

acme-support: thanks, doing that now. They confirmed p99 latency drop back to normal after flip on a small canary.

qa-bot: after adding the golden-case to the suite, CI should block the merge if it regresses again. Make sure to include both permissive and strict mode expectations in tests.

eval-bot: suggested test cases to add: 1) templated-json-number-fields 2) nested-array-number-coercion 3) tool-selection-ambiguity leading to unexpected schema. I've uploaded golden prompts and expected parsed arg JSON to the eval bucket: gs://evals/goldens/toolcall/2025-06-10-acme-order.json

derek: quick notes for the PR: - change is small, add coercion where schema type==number -> try int/float conversion - add unit tests (positive + negative) - add telemetry metric `toolcall.coercions` to track how often we coerce - add fallback to strict parse if coercion fails.

elena: patch pushed to `rtf-hotfix/perm_coerce_nums` and canary deployed to us-west-2. Sam, can you coordinate with Acme to run their full job against the canary endpoint?

sam: coordinating now. Acme ran the job and reports success for the order pipeline and tokens normalized. They did a run for ~1500 orders; p95/p99 back to baseline.

maya: closing loop: will file an incident follow-up and add postmortem steps. Action items: Derek to PR coercion + tests, Elena to add per-tenant toggle + logging hook, Sam to confirm billing anomaly resolved and capture invoice snapshot, QA to add golden prompts into `toolcall-schema-suite`.

derek: PR in flight: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rtf/pull/4128 — includes tests and metric.

elena: leaving a note: long-term we should avoid relying on text-parsing for structured args where possible; prefer typed function payload field in the wire format. Filed an RFC: https://go.redwood.ai/rfc/typed-tool-args

maya: thanks all. tagging for postmortem: @derek @elena @sam @qa-bot @eval-bot :thumbsup:

acme-support: thanks team! appreciate the fast turnaround.
